visibility: evaluator-private; never inject into model context
membership_notation:
(resolved by the oracle at run time, never sent to the model):
  {"rule": "ranked", "top_n": 3, "rank_by": "orders"}
  {"rule": "fixed", "from": "H1:v1"}            members displayed by v1 in setup snapshot H1
  {"rule": "fixed", "from": "after:T5:v1"}      members displayed by v1 after turn 5 committed
  {"rule": "fixed", "from": "played:T2"}        categories named in the PLAYED part of turn 2
                                                (human-coded from played-sample cutoff)

scenarios.title: Seasonal reuse: first-quarter categories in the third quarter
scenarios.goal: Compare service quality for the categories that led in Q1 against the current Q3 period in RJ.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What changed between the first quarter and now?
turns.note: Discussion only; reading history must not restore it.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.constraint: Compares H1 and current; must not edit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Put the first-quarter categories into charts two and three, but keep the third quarter.
turns.note: Historical members only; Q1 dates must NOT return.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Chart one too.
turns.note: Elliptical retarget: same operation, add v1.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, no, leave chart one showing this quarter's own top three.
turns.note: Undo of the previous turn for v1 only, expressed as a rule, not Undo.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show chart one as revenue.
turns.note: Measure only; v1 stays this quarter's top three by orders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And rank it by revenue too.

scenarios.title: Release a fixed set, then change and restore one ranking rule
scenarios.goal: MG charts still carry RJ's fixed categories; the analyst wants MG's own leaders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which categories are these?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.constraint: Names the fixed RJ members; may say they are fixed.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Release the fixed categories and show Minas Gerais' own top three by orders, in all three charts.
turns.note: Known ASR risk: 'Release' heard as 'These'.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Rank chart three by delivery time instead.
turns.note: Ranking criterion only; v3 metric unchanged.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No wait, keep chart three ranked by orders like the others.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Make it the top five in chart one only.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, top four.

scenarios.title: Replace a measure, abandon a half-spoken change, then rank one view
scenarios.goal: Look at revenue for the frozen SP cohort without disturbing the service views.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Change chart one to revenue, keep everything else.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, also chart three, show it for shipped orders. No, delivered is right, leave it.
turns.note: Self-repair that ends in no change. Any status edit on v3 is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Now rank chart one by revenue, top five.
turns.note: Ranking releases v1's fixed set only; v2/v3 keep the fixed cohort.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Put charts two and three on the second half of 2017.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Keep the same categories there.
turns.note: Retention confirmation; re-ranking v2/v3 is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And chart one too, same half.

scenarios.title: Backchannels during an explanation must not edit
scenarios.goal: Listen to an explanation with natural acknowledgements, then narrow the view.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Explain why chart two looks high for one category.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.constraint: Long explanation (>8 s) so that backchannels land inside playback.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mm-hm.
turns.note: Current runtime revokes on every onset; record whether playback was cut and whether the explanation resumed. Any chart change is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, right.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Got it. Narrow all three to the top three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Switch to Minas Gerais.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mm-hm, and chart two by revenue.
turns.note: Starts with an acknowledgement but is a request; must not be held as a backchannel.

scenarios.title: Keep only the categories the assistant has already said
scenarios.goal: Stop a spoken list part-way and freeze exactly the items heard so far.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Read me the five categories in chart one, from the largest.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.constraint: Lists five category names in rank order.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Stop, keep just the ones you've said so far, in all three charts.
turns.note: THE full-duplex case. Inject after the 3rd category name has PLAYED (use playback receipts, not generated text). Truth = names in the played prefix; using all five, or names generated but not played, is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Switch to the second half of 2017.
turns.note: Frozen members kept; ranking must not return.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Read me the delivery times for those.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Change chart one to revenue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Leave the categories frozen.

scenarios.title: Self-repair inside a date request, then a question that sounds like an edit
scenarios.goal: Compare Q3 service metrics; decide later whether order volume follows.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show the second quarter, sorry, third quarter of 2017 in charts two and three.
turns.note: Q2 dates anywhere is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And chart one stays the full year, right?
turns.note: Yes/no question. Editing v1 is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually put chart one on the same quarter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Now the fourth quarter for all three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, sorry, just charts two and three; chart one stays in the third quarter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Is chart three still the delivery time?

scenarios.title: An utterance split by a pause
scenarios.goal: Bring SP's earlier leaders into MG service views, with natural hesitations.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For charts two and three... use the categories from the São Paulo chart we looked at first.
turns.note: 900 ms pause > 600 ms VAD silence. The first fragment alone must not produce a response or edit. MG must stay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Keep Minas Gerais... and the dates too.
turns.note: Confirmation of retention; any edit is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Change chart one to low-review rate.
turns.note: v1 keeps top-3-by-orders membership; rank_by stays orders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Chart one... back to orders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And for all three, only canceled... no, keep delivered orders.
turns.note: Any status change is an error.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Use the first quarter of 2017 for charts two and three.

scenarios.title: Barge-in while the tool is still running
scenarios.goal: Move service views to 2018 while order volume stays in 2017.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Compare all three charts for 2018 instead.
turns.note: Intermediate state; superseded by T2 for v1.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Only charts two and three, leave chart one in 2017.
turns.note: If T1 already committed, v1 must be explicitly restored to 2017 (a legal earlier commit stays legal). If T1 was revoked before commit, v2/v3 still need 2018.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.constraint: Must say which charts changed and that chart one is 2017.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Use their own top three by orders in 2018.
turns.note: 'their' = charts two and three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Make charts one and two revenue.
turns.note: Intermediate; superseded by the next turn for chart two.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Only chart one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And show chart one for 2018 as well.

scenarios.title: Wrong chart named, then corrected
scenarios.goal: Revenue belongs on the order view; align delivery view to the same cohort.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Change chart two to revenue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, I meant chart one, not two. Put chart two back to low-review rate.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And give chart three the same categories as chart one.
turns.note: Source is the CURRENT chart one, not history; v3 top-5 ranking released.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good. Leave it there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, rank chart three by its own top five orders again.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Top three, not five.

scenarios.title: Swap cohorts and come back to the first one
scenarios.goal: Decide between RJ and SP leaders for an MG service review.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which region did these categories come from?
turns.note: Correct answer: São Paulo (H2). Tests provenance, not computation.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Swap them for the Rio ones.
turns.note: MG stays.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, the São Paulo set was better. Go back to that, but keep the current dates.
turns.note: 'Go back' is not Undo/restore of a whole version.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And only the first half.
turns.note: Targets inherited from the previous turn (charts two and three).

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show the same for chart one, but keep it ranked.
turns.note: 'the same' = first half; v1 keeps its MG top-3 ranking.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which set are charts two and three using now?
turns.note: Correct answer: the São Paulo set (H2).

scenarios.title: Ambiguous 'those three' must trigger a question
scenarios.goal: Choose between RJ historical leaders and MG current leaders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Use those three categories in the service charts.
turns.note: Ambiguous: RJ historical top 3 vs MG current top 3. Expect one short question; any edit is a premature commit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The Rio ones.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Keep chart one as the local top three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show charts two and three for São Paulo, same categories.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And chart one too, São Paulo's own top three.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Use the same three in all charts... I mean the Rio ones.
turns.note: Self-repair resolves 'the same three' to the RJ set; v1 stays in SP.

scenarios.title: Change order status without re-selecting categories
scenarios.goal: Check canceled-order volume for the frozen SP cohort, then return to revenue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show chart one for canceled orders instead of delivered.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Leave the categories as they are.
turns.note: Fixed set must not be re-ranked for canceled orders.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Charts two and three stay on delivered.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually switch chart one back to delivered and make it revenue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show charts two and three for 2018.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hmm, only the first half of 2018.

scenarios.title: Change grouping dimension and come back
scenarios.goal: See where the SP cohort's orders come from, then analyse it in MG.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For chart one, break these categories down by customer state, all of Brazil.
turns.note: Fixed categories become a filter; region cleared.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show it by month instead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, back to categories, Minas Gerais.
turns.note: Fixed SP cohort retained under MG.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Show chart two by month for these categories, all of Brazil.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, chart two only for São Paulo.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Back to categories for chart two.

scenarios.title: Stacked elliptical edits, then freeze the current set
scenarios.goal: Compare RJ order leaders with MG service quality for the same categories.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Make all three charts top five.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And Minas Gerais.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Wait, keep chart one in Rio.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And freeze the Rio categories from chart one into charts two and three.
turns.note: Members = RJ top 5 shown by v1 after T5; v2/v3 stay MG.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Now the first half of 2017 for everything.
turns.note: v1 is still a dynamic ranking, so its members may change; v2/v3 stay frozen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: But don't let chart one re-rank; keep the categories it had.
turns.note: Members = v1's full-year RJ top five before the date change; H1 dates kept.

scenarios.title: Hypotheticals, polite requests and 'fix it'
scenarios.goal: Move order volume to revenue and service views to Q4.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if we used revenue in chart one?
turns.note: Hypothetical. Editing now is a premature commit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, do it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Could chart three show the last quarter of 2017?
turns.note: Polite request = edit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fix it so chart two matches.
turns.note: Match = dates only; v2 metric unchanged.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What would chart one look like for Rio?
turns.note: Hypothetical; editing now is a premature commit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the other two as well.

scenarios.title: Cumulative flow (replicates the failed 2026-11-13 run)
scenarios.goal: Reuse RJ leaders in MG service views, narrow time, then release one view.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Give me a quick read of the three charts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Bring the Rio categories into charts two and three, keep Minas Gerais.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Just the first half.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: No, first quarter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Now drop the Rio set in chart two and show its own top three by orders.
turns.note: v3 keeps RJ members and Q1.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Change chart three to revenue.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Keep the Rio set there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And put chart one on the first quarter too.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Done, thanks.
turns.note: Closing; any edit is an error.
